No. Mailwing wraps your provider's own web interface in an isolated session per account — Gmail talks to Google, Outlook talks to Microsoft, and so on. Mailwing itself never sees your messages and routes nothing through any intermediary.

q: Is Mailwing signed and safe to open?
a: On macOS, yes — Mailwing is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so it opens with a normal double-click. On Windows there's no code-signing certificate yet, so SmartScreen still shows a one-time "More info → Run anyway" step on first launch. Either way, every build is produced in the open by GitHub Actions, so you can audit exactly what shipped.

q: Can I add a provider that isn't on the list?
a: Most webmail providers work if you can pin them — open an issue on GitHub with the provider URL and we'll look at adding it to the registry.
No, and there are no plans. Mailwing is intentionally a desktop app for people who do email at a keyboard. Use your provider's own mobile app for phone access.

q: Does Mailwing sync between my computers?
a: No. Accounts and notes live only on the machine where you added them. If you want them on another computer, sign in there too.
